batch: C03d.1 analytic current impulse derivatives through every FFT window

environment.native_features: Default features for rspice-core, rspice-results and rspice-simulation.

source_hash_scope: Working-tree bytes for every file in the implementation commit and dependency/toolchain locks.

implementation.shared_window_law: Finite samples and analytic derivatives share canonical nonnegative sine-polynomial windows. Reflection preserves small endpoint distances; Hann/Blackman/Cosine4/Sine6 no longer lose representable endpoint weights to cosine cancellation. Gaussian and Kaiser retain their authored alpha conventions.
implementation.derivatives: Leibniz derivatives combine raw analytic window derivatives with the complex exponential at the exact retained event time. Polynomial convolution, a Gaussian recurrence and a positive hypergeometric Kaiser derivative series use retained binary exponents and exact product sums. Rectangular windows keep their logarithmic-order fast path.
implementation.public_route: Engine::evaluate_transient_fft_results uses the same preflight and evaluation as transient post-processing. Finite samples, ordinary charge impulses and higher current derivatives combine before normalization and metrics, including affine current/voltage expressions.
implementation.boundaries: Ownership is (START,STOP]. Periodic windows wrap at STOP; symmetric windows have compact support through the last sample. Classical derivatives are evaluated where they exist. Genuine triangular corners and insufficiently smooth support boundaries return explicit errors. A normalized interior coordinate that rounds onto a boundary also returns a distinct numerical error.
implementation.resources: Checked workspace accounting, fallible vector reserves and bounded-stride cancellation cover derivative accumulation. A filtered-term regression limits work before cancellation. Resource refusal and cancellation preserve subsequent reuse.
implementation.runtime_admission: The transition kernel remains cfg(test); no physical event provider generates higher derivatives, H-family event admission remains absent, and checkpoint identity remains v105.

coverage.independent_oracle: mpmath 1.3.0 differentiates the original cosine/Bessel definitions at 100 decimal digits, independently of production polynomial jets and Kaiser recurrence. 400 spectra / 2000 complex coefficients cover all 16 windows, both window conventions, orders 1/2/3/5/8 and positions 5/16 and 11/16. Gaussian/Kaiser alpha values are 1/3/20. Eight points, START=0.5, duration=1.25 and coefficient=-1e-6.
coverage.gates: Complex error <2e-12*max(reference norm,1e-30); coherent gain relative error <2e-14. Separate cases cover support endpoints, corners, affine weighting, finite samples plus charge plus derivatives, normalized/unnormalized output and metrics.
coverage.range: Five taper families preserve compensating duration/coefficient scales (1e-150,1e-300) and (1e150,1e300) for order two. u32::MAX order receives bounded typed refusal; an order-128 Kaiser operation can be cancelled and a subsequent operation succeeds.
coverage.scope: Selected native tests and five optimized WASM integration tests; no all-order/all-parameter or full-core qualification, benchmark, public CCVS solve, external-model/JIT execution or product-readiness claim.
